title: ui.setHeader / ui.setFooter stop swallowing silently, and hook widgets get an owner
wave: Wave 6 of 8 in M2. TWO PRs, and they are gated differently. PR 1 = the two throw sites + `test/extension-ui-header-footer.test.ts`; this is the only thing the wave-6 gate runs. PR 2 = the owner half (per-extension widget maps + per-extension UI context + remount instead of global wipe); it is NOT gated at wave 6, but it MUST land before WI-9 (wave 7) so WI-9's 11-bucket unload inventory has something to enumerate.
one_line: An extension author who calls `ctx.ui.setHeader(...)` — on the TUI or on a headless run — now gets a real error naming the method and pointing at `setWidget`/`setEditorComponent` instead of nothing at all; and every hook widget is filed under the extension that set it, so removing one extension no longer takes everyone else's widget with it and pressing `/new` no longer blanks a still-running extension's widget.
user_visible_effect: Two things a user can actually notice. (1) An extension whose author used `ui.setHeader`/`ui.setFooter` fails loudly — either the panel appears or the extension's own call surfaces an error naming `setHeader` plus the two methods that do work — instead of silently drawing nothing and leaving the author with no debug handle. (2) Running `/new` or switching sessions no longer makes a still-running extension's widget vanish from the frame, and removing one extension no longer strips a different extension's widget. PR 1 alone delivers only (1); (2) needs PR 2.
effort: PR 1 (throw sites + wave-6 test file): S. Two object-literal members become throwing methods, one shared error-message helper, one new test file of two rows. PR 2 (owner half): M, not S. The widget maps change shape, the TUI `uiContext` object literal becomes a factory, `ExtensionRunner` gains a new per-extension context constructor, and the global wipe becomes a per-extension remount across FIVE call sites spread over two byte-identical duplicated handler blocks. PR 2 is only M-sized if you also retain the widget's factory/content — see the plan_corrections entry on that, because the current maps discard it and a remount is otherwise impossible.
risk: The single most likely way to get this wrong is shipping PR 1 and closing the wave. The silent calls become honest, §11.1's fifth test goes green, and the frame still holds widgets belonging to an extension that was removed, while `clearHookWidgets()` still wipes a running extension's widget every time the user presses `/new`. The second most likely is fixing `extension-ui-controller.ts:157-158` and stopping there: the plan says there are two silent sites, there are FOUR, and the other three are `runner.ts:424-425`, `session/agent-session.ts:540-541` and `acp-agent.ts:581-582`. The wave-6 test rows would still go green, because row (1) runs on a UI context and never touches a no-frame context, and row (2) only reaches the runner's copy. This is why the gate's grep clause counts hits rather than trusting the two rows. Third: editing only one of the two duplicated `newSession`/`switchSession` handler blocks — they are byte-identical today, so a partial fix produces a silent behavioral split no test can see. Fourth: treating the ACP site as an oversight rather than a decision, because its own JSDoc documents the silence as intentional.
blocks: WI-9 (wave 7) — the owner half of PR 2 must land first, or WI-9's unload inventory has no way to enumerate or release hook widgets. This is §5.1 H: land before WI-9.

plan_corrections.claim: Plan §WI-13: 'Sau khi widget có owner, cú quét không còn được xoá toàn cục nữa: nó trở thành remount theo từng extension — `dispose()` widget cũ rồi gọi lại factory của nó để dựng widget mới trên session vừa mở.'
plan_corrections.verdict: GAP — the plan's remount is not implementable against the current data structure; this is the one thing most likely to burn an engineer
plan_corrections.correction: The two maps store the RENDERED COMPONENT, not the content/factory. `#hookWidgetsAbove = new Map<string, ExtensionUiComponent>()` (`:87`) and `#hookWidgetsBelow` (`:88`), and `setHookWidget` does `target.set(key, this.#createHookWidget(content))` (`:354`) — `content` is a local that goes out of scope. `#createHookWidget` (`:364-379`) turns a `string[]` into a fresh `Container` of `Text` children, so for array content the original lines are gone entirely. There is nothing to re-invoke, so 'remount by calling the factory again' cannot be written without first changing what the map holds. PR 2 must change the value type to carry the content alongside the component — e.g. `Map<extensionPath, Map<string, { content: ExtensionWidgetContent; component: ExtensionUiComponent }>>` — and `#createHookWidget`/`#removeHookWidget`/`#renderHookWidgetContainer` updated to read `.component` while remount re-reads `.content`. Also note `ExtensionUiComponent` is `Component & { dispose?(): void }` (`packages/tui/src/chat/extension-types.ts:5`), so `dispose` is optional: remount must call `dispose?.()`, matching the existing `#removeHookWidget` at `:359`.

plan_corrections.verdict: WRONG — there are FOUR, and they do not all share the same intent
plan_corrections.correction: `grep -rn 'setFooter: () => {}\|setHeader: () => {}' packages/coding-agent/src` returns EIGHT lines = four distinct sites, not two. (a) `modes/controllers/extension-ui-controller.ts:157-158` — the TUI path, the plan's site 1. (b) `extensibility/extensions/runner.ts:424-425` — `noOpUIContext`, the plan's site 2. (c) `session/agent-session.ts:540-541` — a SECOND, entirely separate `noOpUIContext` declared at `:518` and used at `:7400`, which the plan never mentions. It is a genuine extension-facing fallback: `#createCommandContext()` returns `{ ui: noOpUIContext, mode: 'print', hasUI: false, ... }` when the session has no extension runner, so an extension command handler in a hand-constructed session gets this context and its `setHeader` call is swallowed. Its own JSDoc at `:7404-7406` notes the path is reached only by hand-constructed sessions, but it is still reachable and still silent. (d) `modes/acp/acp-agent.ts:581-582` — inside the exported `createAcpExtensionUiContext(connection, getSessionId, clientCapabilities)` declared at `:425`. This one is DIFFERENT IN KIND: its own JSDoc at `:409-424` deliberately documents the silence ('The non-elicitation surface (custom components, theming, terminal input) remains stubbed — ACP clients render those themselves or not at all'). Consequence for the plan: its failure-mode-4 warning ('fix the controller, forget the runner, gate stays green') is still right but understates the exposure by 2x, and the plan's remedy — 'both sites are in WI-13's scope' — is not a decision that can be made mechanically, because (c) is a bug and (d) is a documented design choice. See the ACP open question.

open_questions: Option (A) vs (B) is not yet a decision, it is a recommendation. The plan recommends (B) — make both throw and point at the two methods that work — and I have found no evidence anyone accepted it. Confirm in writing before PR 1 starts. If (A) is chosen instead, `packages/tui` gains new public API and §4.2 must be amended explicitly; it must not slip in as an implementation detail.

Session-switch behavior: the plan mandates remount (dispose the old widget, re-invoke the factory on the newly opened session). Confirm that is right, because it means a widget factory is called more than once per session and a factory closing over session state must tolerate that. The alternative — keeping the widget across the switch without re-invoking — is not what the plan says, so do not drift into it without a decision.

Widget key collision across two extensions. The plan says a collision must be 'reported, not silently overwritten', but does not say what 'reported' means. Options: `logger.warn` and last-writer-wins; or reject the second call the same way `setHeader` now throws. Test row (5) has to assert one specific outcome, so this must be settled before the row is written.

Does `setStatus` get per-extension ownership in the same PR? `setHookStatus` at `extension-ui-controller.ts:591-592` forwards to `this.ctx.statusLine.setHookStatus(key, text)`, and the status line keeps its own key map outside this controller. It is out of WI-13's stated scope, but it means `setWidget` and `setStatus` will have different collision and ownership semantics after PR 2. That asymmetry should be a decision, not an accident.

Test row (3) ('the widget actually appears in the frame') needs a fixture loaded through `discoverAndLoadExtensions(configuredPaths, cwd, eventBus?, disabledExtensionIds?, options?)` — `packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/loader.ts:668-677`. The plan says 'an extension fixture' without saying whether it must be the out-of-repo `outsider-extension` fixture from §11.2 item 12 (which does not exist yet) or a test-local temp fixture. Pick one; if it is the outsider fixture, row (3) is blocked behind item 12 and belongs in wave 7 with the other two rows, not wave 6.

ACP mode is a scope decision, not a mechanical fix. `createAcpExtensionUiContext` (`modes/acp/acp-agent.ts:425`) stubs `setHeader`/`setFooter` at `:581-582`, and its own JSDoc at `:409-424` says that surface 'remains stubbed — ACP clients render those themselves or not at all'. So there are two defensible answers: (i) ACP has no frame, so it should throw the same no-frame message as the other non-TUI paths and the JSDoc gets updated; or (ii) ACP genuinely has a frame concept owned by the client, in which case silence is correct and the JSDoc stays, but then §11.1's fifth test is not satisfied on ACP and that has to be written down. Option (i) is the one consistent with the rest of this work item, but it is a behavior change to a documented mode and must be decided, not assumed. The gate clause below assumes (i).

The no-UI-path message must be different: it has to say the current mode has no frame at all and tell the author to guard the call with `ctx.hasUI`, because at that call site a frame IS available and the call fails for a different reason. Reusing one message for both is the exact failure the plan warns about.

test_contract:
Two things, both observable from outside the implementation, and neither is 'the function was called'.

Row (1) — negative contract, UI-backed. An extension context backed by a real frame calls `ui.setHeader(factory)` and `ui.setFooter(factory)`. The call must NOT return silently. Either the component appears in the frame (option A) or the call throws; under the recommended option (B) it throws, and the message names the method that was actually called plus BOTH of `setWidget` and `setEditorComponent`. If someone regresses this to a silent no-op, an extension author's panel vanishes with no error anywhere — which is the exact failure this work item exists to kill. Note the assertion is on the THROW and its content, never on internal wiring.

Row (2) — negative contract, no-UI path. A runner that was never initialized with a UI context hands extensions `noOpUIContext`. Calling `ui.setHeader(...)` on it must also throw, and the message must tell the author to guard with `ctx.hasUI` — a different remedy than row (1), because at that call site there is no frame at all. The test additionally asserts `hasUI()` is false, which is what proves the row exercised `noOpUIContext` and not the TUI literal. Consumer impact if it regresses: on RPC, print, and JSON modes — the modes where a user has the least visibility — the call is swallowed again and the author has no debug handle whatsoever. This row is not observable from row (1)'s harness, which is why omitting it leaves the wave gate green with half the bug still in the tree.

What this file does NOT cover, and must not be made to look like it does: that a widget actually appears in the frame; that removing one extension removes only its widget (this genuinely fails on HEAD today); and that two extensions on the same key are reported rather than silently overwriting. Those three rows belong to `test/extension-unload.test.ts` under WI-9, whose verification command already runs that file. Wave 6 shipping with only rows (1) and (2) is 4/5 of §11.1's fifth capability — the exact state §11.2 item 11 exists to prevent being mistaken for done.

gate:
PR 1 (this is the wave-6 gate) is DONE when all four hold. (a) `bun run check:ts` is green. (b) `bun test test/extension-ui-header-footer.test.ts` reports 2 passing tests. (c) `grep -rn 'setFooter: () => {}\|setHeader: () => {}' packages/coding-agent/src` returns ZERO hits — no silent pair survives anywhere, at any of the four sites. (If the ACP open question is decided as 'ACP's silence is correct', clause (c) narrows to three sites and the decision must be recorded in the PR; it must not be narrowed silently.) (d) The two tests were each observed to FAIL on HEAD before the fix; if they passed on HEAD they are proving nothing.

The gate CAN go red on a partial fix, which is the property that makes it worth having. Fixing only `extension-ui-controller.ts:157-158` and missing the other three leaves six hits and clause (c) does not pass. Reverting either throwing site to a silent no-op makes clause (b) fail, because both tests call methods that must throw. Clause (d) is what separates a real gate from a decorative one: a test that passes on HEAD proves nothing, so both rows must be run against HEAD first.

The one thing the wave-6 gate CANNOT catch is the missing owner half. If PR 1 ships and PR 2 is never started, every clause above is satisfied, §11.1's fifth test goes green, and the frame still holds widgets belonging to extensions that were removed, while `/new` still blanks a running extension's widget. That gap is closed by the §5.1 H ordering constraint (land before WI-9), which is a human check, not a command.

PR 2 (owner half, lands before WI-9) is DONE when: `bun run check:ts` is green, PR 1's two tests still pass, the widget maps are per-extension with content retained, all FIVE remount call sites were converted (controller :246, :307, :478, :536 and interactive-mode :6020 — count them, do not eyeball them), the comment block at runner.ts:756-777 no longer contradicts the new optional parameter, and the manual `/new` check in step 14 was performed and reported.
